key_insight: A geometric invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) formulation enables curvature-driven surface-flow schemes with unconditional discrete energy decay, independent of the chosen tangential motion.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports energy-stable finite element simulation of evolving interfaces governed by curvature- and orientation-dependent energies.
method: Introduce a square-root auxiliary variable to express the geometric energy as a quadratic functional.
Combine auxiliary-variable evolution with skew-symmetric surface transport.
Construct monolithic nonlinear parametric FEM schemes with BGN or minimal-deformation-rate tangential velocities.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments demonstrating robustness and accuracy, alongside unconditional discrete energy-decay estimates for both schemes.
watch_item: Unconditional energy decay does not establish time-step-independent accuracy; the schemes also require monolithic nonlinear solves.
paper_title: A geometric-IEQ approach for curvature-driven flows
